events.text:
## Recommendation
- Go to **St. Joseph** for pier salmon this week. I'd rate it about **1 (below average)**.
- Expect slow pier fishing at **South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon**. I'd rate each about **0 (slow)**.
- At St. Joseph, fish spawn on the bottom. Spawn was the only pier lure reported there.
- Check the pier and the wind before you go. I don't have a live wind forecast or pierhead water reading for this week.

## Why
- The newest St. Joseph pier report (Apr 26) said a few coho were caught on bottom-fished spawn, which is the best pier result of the recent reports.
- Muskegon and South Haven both had pier reports rated slow on Apr 26, and Muskegon's Apr 20 pier report was also slow.
- I'd expect Grand Haven to be slow too: its newest report (Apr 20) said dirty Grand River water had slowed the action.
- Past years at similar water temperature (about 46 F) show pier fishing mostly slow to average, with St. Joseph's pier usually the better of these ports (past seasons, see Evidence).

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is 2023-04-26, six days old)
- St. Joseph, 2023-04-26: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho using spawn fished on the bottom." Rated 1 (below average). Boats were catching coho in 10 to 60 feet of water.
- St. Joseph, 2023-04-12: "Pier anglers and shore anglers were catching decent numbers of coho. … Most fish were caught on spawn fished on the bottom." Rated 2 (average). This is three weeks old.
- South Haven, 2023-04-26: "Pier fishing was slow for coho." Rated 0 (slow). There was no South Haven pier report on Apr 12.
- Muskegon, 2023-04-26: "Pier anglers found the action to be very slow for brown trout and coho salmon." Rated 0 (slow). The Apr 20 Muskegon pier report was also slow, and said "A few were caught on spawn."
- Grand Haven, 2023-04-20: "Dirty water from the Grand River has slowed the action for brown trout and coho salmon." Rated 0 (slow). The newest Grand Haven report is 12 days old, and its pier results are from Apr 12 (rated 1), so the pier picture there is thin.

**Past seasons** (same time of year, surface water near 46 F)
- St. Joseph, 2022-05-04: "Pier fishing was difficult due to the rough weather. … There were a few coho being caught on spawn." Rated 1. Boats did better there, with coho good in 30 feet of water.
- South Haven, 2022-05-04: pier coho on spawn, "a few," rated 1.
- South Haven, 2022-04-20: "Pier fishing was very slow for coho and trout." Rated 0.
- These are history, not this week's reports.

**Conditions now**
- The live feed was unavailable for today. The latest week in the data (ending 2023-05-02) had buoy surface water of 45 to 46 F at all four ports: St. Joseph 46 F (flat), South Haven 46 F (−1 F), Grand Haven 45 F (−3 F), Muskegon 45 F (−3 F). These are measured buoy readings.
- The data had no modeled pierhead water and no wind forecast, so I can't say whether an upwelling is under way.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): north or east winds can push cold water toward piers and river mouths. A sharp drop in surface temperature signals this. The drops at Grand Haven and Muskegon (−3 F each) are not large, but I can't confirm an upwelling from them.

## Caveats
- The newest pier report is from Apr 26, six days old. Early-season pier fishing changes quickly, so treat these ratings as a guide.
- The pier ratings are my estimates from thin data. South Haven and Grand Haven have no pier reports from the most recent week.
- No live wind or pierhead water data was available, so check the forecast and the pier before you go.
- Holland had no current report and is not included here.

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, 2023-04-20: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3561fa6
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph, 2023-04-12: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3548e2b
- Past seasons, 2022-05-04 (St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
